page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 180 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix and vector operations. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-48 demonstrates strong performance in compute-heavy and instruction-set-dependent workloads. It achieves a Passmark CPU score of 54,598.51 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18,084.0, both placing in the strong tier. The hardware-assisted matrix and vector extensions contribute to top-tier performance in image processing and text processing, alongside strong performance in software compilation and ray tracing. Single-threaded and multi-threaded decompression tasks via bzip3 also register in the strong category, reaching 14.47 GB/sec and 288.36 GB/sec respectively. Memory performance is balanced, with uncached read bandwidth at 144.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 61.98 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-48 offers high compute density and specialized instruction sets, making it highly efficient for workloads that can leverage AMX and AVX-512 without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and bundled GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data and limiting its suitability for massive parallel GPU-accelerated tasks. The instance is well-suited for CPU-based machine learning inference, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose compute workloads that require a balanced memory-to-core ratio.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 180 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. It features 24 physical cores with hyper-threading, a 260 MB L3 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Lacking local storage and GPUs, the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage. In benchmarks, it delivers strong multi-core performance, particularly in image processing, text processing, and software compilation. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in CPU-based LLM inference, such as processing 198.07 tokens per second on medium 7B models. The c4-standard-48 is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference where dedicated GPU acceleration is not required.
